posts.meta_description:
elleindia on November 11, 2025: "#ELLECoverStar: When Nidhi Sunil (@nidhisunil) first appeared on the cover of ELLE India back in 2011, she was unsuspecting of where her life’s twists and turns would eventually lead her. Too dark, too short—people were quick to label her in outmoded parrot tones. “But that cover was special. Your team didn’t edit my skin. I looked like my true South Indian self,” she recalls. Sunil is easily one of our finest exports to the west—which Indian model can boast of a L'Oreal Paris contract in her kitty?! Back in 2021, she became the first Indian model to achieve this feat. Over the years, she has fronted numerous international campaigns, enjoyed the world of high-fashion editorials and used her global platform to advocate for diversity and ethical beauty. Head to the 🔗 in bio to read the full conversation with our cover star.
____________________________________
On @nidhisunil: LOVE unlimited bracelets and rings, all by @cartier. Small panel asymmetric dress by @louisvuitton.
____________________________________
Editorial Director: Ainee Nizami Ahmedi (@aineenizamiahmedi)
Photographer: Raajadharshini (@raajadharshini)
Fashion Director: Zoha Castelino (@zohacastelino)
Asst. Art Director: Alekha Chugani (@alekhachuganii)
Makeup: Sandhya Shekhar (@sandhyashekar)
Hair: Umang Thapa (@umang.artist) rep by Anima (@animacreatives) 
Bookings Editor: Rishith Shetty (@rishithvshetty)
Words by: Ipsita Kaul (@ipsitakaul)
Assisted by: Tejashree Raul (@tejashreeraul), Anshu Sheth (@uncultured.by.anshu) (styling), Sharayu Karalkar (@sharayukaralkar) (bookings)
Airline Partner: Emirates (@emirates)
________________________________________
Read the full story in ELLE India’s new issue.
________________________________
#ELLECovers #NidhiSunil #IndianModels".

14K likes, 556 comments - nidhisunil on November 5, 2021: "Take up space. Take up space. Take up space. I’ve had some dark moments in modelling but this is not one of them. This one is for all the brown girls in India that didn’t feel like there was place at the table. I’m not winning you are ❤️ #Repost @vogueindia Defying stereotypes while amplifying inclusivity, Nidhi Sunil (@nidhisunil), model, activist and all-round outspoken citizen of the world, is turning the fashion industry upside down with her subversive career trajectory. The spirited globetrotter is among the trio of cover stars shot exclusively for Vogue India’s Women of the Year issue that celebrates noteworthy achievements made by women across various fields. Head to the link in bio to read more about our November 2021 cover star. #VogueWOTY2021

On Nidhi: Bodysuit, Saint Laurent (@ysl); Earrings, Helene Zubeldia (@helenezubeldia)

Photographer: Pierre Debusschere (@pierredebusschere). Styled by Priyanka Kapadia (@priyankarkapadia). Words by Avanti Dalal (@avantidalal)

Photographer's agency: Art+Commerce (@artandcommerce). Styling assistant: Naheed Driver (@naheedee); Manavi Dang (@manavidang). Make-up: Adrien Pinault (@@adrienpinault)/ M+A (@maworldgroup). Hair: Peter Gray (@@petergrayhair)/Home
Digital Technician: Stefano Poli (@@ stefano_p_o_l_i)/ Digitart Paris. Photo Assistant: Peter Keyser (@peter_keyser); Patricia Zheng (@patricia.zhg). Production: Johanne Olessen (@johanneuhrenholtolesen); New Light Films (@newlightfilms)

Visuals Editor: Jay Modi (@jaymodi2). Art Director: Snigdha Kulkarni (@snigdhakulkarni_). Entertainment Director: Megha Mehta (@magzmehta)".

posts.meta_description: 3,944 likes, 95 comments - nidhisunil on April 24, 2023: "We’re beatboxers, chief ministers, police officers, civil service officers, lawyers, doctors, actors, social workers…you name it. From the outside looking in, i’m the one doing the helping, but the truth is i’ve always been the one being helped. I have always walked away with more perspective, joy, gratitude, inspiration and more of a sense of connectedness to community and life in general, than I arrived with. Its a privilege for me to work for these angels in disguise ❤️ 900 and counting. As always consider helping by sponsoring a girl or becoming a donor or just spreading the word🥰".

143 likes, 15 comments - kateodonnell.ayurveda on August 23, 2026: "@Nidhisunil told me something I keep returning to: after years of constant output, the first thing that helped her sleep again wasn't a prescription. It was dal, rice, and ghee — a bowl of kitchari her body remembered from growing up in Kerala.

In an increasingly successful modeling career, she'd been running on adrenaline through red-eye flights to Paris and back, until burnout stopped her completely. Insomnia. Panic. Total depletion. What brought her back was food, rest, and eventually a whole new relationship with her own worth.
This one is for anyone who's been extracting from themselves for too long, or anyone who is looking to reframe “self worth.”

And a shout out to this season’s sponsors @drtungs, @banyanbotanicals, and @banyanfarmlife for helping us get important information like this out there!

Listen to the pod Everyday Ayurveda with Kate wherever you get your podcasts. Please subscribe, review, and help me keep producing these.

#AyurvedaPodcast #AyurvedaCommunity #Burnout #SelfCare #Transition".

93 likes, 15 comments - kateodonnell.ayurveda on August 19, 2026: "Perfectionism disguised as wellness. @nidhisunil calls a spade a spade.

Vogue India's Model of the Year, the first Indian face of L'Oréal and women’s advocate @nidhisunil calls out some BS in this episode. There is so much I never knew about the modeling industry. 

This week Nidhi Sunil joins me for one of the most honest conversations we've had on this show — about burnout, self-worth, and the slow work of coming back to yourself. It started, of all places, with a bowl of kitchari.

And a shout out to this season’s sponsors @drtungs, @banyanbotanicals, and @banyanfarmlife for helping us get important information like this out there!

Listen to the pod Everyday Ayurveda with Kate wherever you get your podcasts. Please subscribe, review, and help me keep producing these.

nidhisunil on March 17, 2026: "The dawn is breaking after the eternal night;
I am grateful for the breaking light:
But i am grateful even more for the eternal night. 

1st slide Yoshida Tōshi, Sunrise, 1989
last slide Chiura Obata, Setting Sun on Sacremento Valley, California, 1930".
